stories.headline: MKBHD Announces Fresh Start with New Video “I’m Starting Over”
stories.summary: Tech YouTuber Marques Brownlee (MKBHD) posted a video titled “I’m Starting Over,” signaling a shift in his content strategy. He hints at revamping his channel’s approach, though details of the changes remain limited in the release.

stories.headline: Basketball Intelligence Newsletter Highlights NBA Power Rankings, Rookie Ladder, and Team Analyses
stories.summary: The November 23, 2026 edition of Basketball Intelligence compiles top NBA reporting, including power rankings for defenses, a rookie ladder, and team-specific notes on matchups like Celtics‑Warriors and Nuggets‑Bulls. Subscribers also get links to deeper analyses from outlets such as ESPN, The Athletic, and Bleacher Report.

stories.headline: Rams Unleash Heavy Dime Schemes to Defy Defensive Norms
stories.summary: Los Angeles Rams defensive coordinator Chris Shula has leaned heavily into Dime packages, utilizing them on 43 percent of snaps despite missing key interior linemen like Poona Ford and Kobie Turner. The unit has successfully stifled the run and held opponents to negative EPA per play when deploying the light package. Shula utilizes the scheme to seamlessly counter modern personnel sets while leaning on versatile sub-package pieces like Trent McDuffie and Quentin Lake.

stories.headline: TGC Explores Integrating Church History Into Modern Ministry
stories.summary: The Gospel Coalition released resources detailing how pastors and leaders can utilize historical church movements to shape contemporary ministry. The essay series addresses traditional theology and foundational figures to guide modern evangelicals. Authors emphasize the value of looking to past church eras to address current spiritual challenges.

stories.headline: Preaching Strategies Tailored for Modern Workers
stories.summary: The Gospel Coalition published guidelines focusing on how faith leaders can effectively communicate spiritual concepts to working-class congregations. The material addresses the disconnect between traditional sermons and daily secular employment. Pastors are encouraged to ground their messages in the realities of daily vocations.

stories.headline: Marques Brownlee Follows Up on Editorial Trust and Integrity
stories.summary: Popular tech creator Marques Brownlee has published the second installment in a series examining whether audiences can trust his product assessments. The release addresses channel credibility and transparency standards across his gadget coverage and review processes.

stories.headline: MKBHD Reviews MacBook Pro LED: Stellar Performance, Not Just Looks
stories.summary: MKBHD calls the new MacBook Pro LED an “incredible laptop,” praising its speed and display while warning viewers not to get distracted by superficial features. The review emphasizes real-world productivity gains over aesthetic hype.

stories.headline: Marques Brownlee Ranks His Favorite Halloween Candy
stories.summary: In a light‑hearted video, Marques Brownlee (Marques Blind) shares his personal ranking of Halloween treats, offering quick commentary on taste, texture, and nostalgic appeal.

stories.headline: Marques’ Studio Spotlights Obscure Foldable Phones
stories.summary: The Studio episode features Marques highlighting a selection of lesser‑known foldable smartphones, explaining their unique designs and why they’ve flown under the mainstream radar.

stories.headline: The Studio Reveals Surprising Gear Behind Its Video Intro
stories.summary: The MKBHD team highlights the unexpected equipment used to capture their video content production intro. The breakdown offers a behind-the-scenes look at their studio's technical setup.

stories.headline: Examining the Cultural Impact of Evening Worship
stories.summary: An essay explores the historical and spiritual weight of evening worship services within the Christian tradition. It reflects on how structured evening liturgies shape faith communities and influence broader cultural practices. The piece serves as a thoughtful meditation for church leaders and believers.

stories.headline: Neil Paine Unveils Data‑Driven 2026‑27 NBA Elo Forecast
stories.summary: Paine releases a season‑long projection for every NBA team using an Elo model calibrated on every game from 1946‑47 to 2024. The system now fits all constants statistically and runs thousands of simulations, generating separate regular‑season and playoff ratings to predict standings, playoff odds and the championship.

stories.headline: 2026 NFL Odds Tracker Offers Full Elo Rankings and QB Value Metrics
stories.summary: Paine’s latest Substack post aggregates market odds, Elo ratings, projected win totals, quarterback EPA scores and in‑season Approximate Value rankings for all NFL clubs. The package includes a meta‑market odds aggregator and historical data spreadsheets for deeper analysis.

stories.headline: GPT‑6.2 Astra Identifies 1808 Sketchbook’s Creator in 22 Minutes
stories.summary: Using minimal prompts, the new Astra model traced an anonymous Yale sketchbook to the vicomte de Chabot by uncovering a little‑known diary reference and recommending a Cleveland State University journal for confirmation. The discovery also yielded a previously unknown source valuable to Canadian and fur‑trade historians.

stories.headline: Review: Kevin DeYoung’s ‘Church History for Everyone’ Makes the Past Accessible
stories.summary: The Gospel Coalition essay evaluates DeYoung’s latest work, arguing that a clear, narrative‑driven approach to church history can equip modern believers with essential context for today’s challenges.

stories.headline: Chinese AI Lab Z.ai Launches GLM-5.4 Featuring Loop Transformer Architecture
stories.summary: Z.ai has released GLM-5.4, its first model utilizing a looped transformer architecture that reuses weight-shared layers for multiple iterations. This design increases network depth without raising the overall parameter count, aiming to enhance complex reasoning tasks like agentic coding.

stories.headline: Ladybird Browser Releases First Alpha, Offering Full Install for macOS and Linux
stories.summary: The Ladybird project unveiled its inaugural alpha build, allowing users to install the self‑contained browser without compiling. Built largely from scratch with its own HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and WebAssembly engines, the alpha runs each tab in a separate process and successfully rendered complex sites, though some WebAssembly‑heavy apps still fail.

stories.headline: Ukrainian Forces Strike Russian Corvette in Libyan Port, Highlighting War’s Global Reach
stories.summary: Ukraine’s SBU coordinated a night‑time attack on the Russian corvette Merkury docked in Benghazi, Libya, marking a rare strike far from the front lines. The operation, praised by President Zelensky, underscores the expanding theater of the conflict, prompting concerns from the UN and Libyan authorities.

stories.headline: The Gospel Coalition Announces 2026 Book Award Finalists
stories.summary: The Gospel Coalition released its annual selections for the 2026 Book Awards, highlighting prominent Christian literature across various categories. The featured list includes essential theological essays, commentaries, and historical studies aimed at church leaders and believers. These selections showcase influential works addressing faith, ministry, and spiritual practice over the past year.

stories.headline: Georgia Upsets No. 1 Florida to Secure SEC Semifinal Spot
stories.summary: The ninth‑seeded Bulldogs knocked out top‑seed Florida 27‑25, 29‑27, 22‑25, 25‑21, marking the program’s highest‑ranked win ever. Bianna Muoneke set a four‑set rally‑scoring record with 28 kills, while Georgia reaches its first SEC semifinal since 2004 and will face Tennessee next.

stories.headline: 2026 College Football Odds Tracker Adds Playoff Forecast and QB PAR Rankings
stories.summary: Paine’s new table lists each team’s market odds, projected wins and chances of making the 12‑team playoff, plus a quarterback Points‑Above‑Replacement rating. An experimental CFP model highlights games that could swing playoff probabilities dramatically.

stories.headline: The Individual Exception: How AI Lets One Person Do the Work of Whole Teams
stories.summary: Ben Thompson details his solo creation of a full studio control system, custom iOS tools and a distributed computing harness, all built with AI assistance. He then contrasts this with historical data showing employee counts at giants like AT&T and IBM have plummeted even as revenue and market cap have surged.

stories.headline: Big Ten Sets Volleyball Semifinals Following Dominant Quarterfinal Sweeps
stories.summary: Top-seeded Nebraska, No. 2 Penn State, No. 3 Wisconsin, and No. 5 Purdue advanced to the inaugural Allstate Big Ten Volleyball Tournament semifinals after winning Sunday's quarterfinals. Nebraska extended its undefeated season to 29-0 by hitting a season-high .488 against Indiana, while Purdue secured the round's only upset by sweeping Oregon. The winners will compete on Wednesday for the conference's automatic NCAA bid.

stories.headline: Amazon Earnings Highlight Compute Strategies and AI Agent Investments
stories.summary: Amazon's latest financial report outlines the company's distinct approach to providing cloud compute and its willingness to sacrifice short-term margins. The analysis explores how tech providers are positioning themselves to serve frontier AI models and autonomous agents. The report also addresses broader industry questions surrounding chip supply and infrastructure scalability.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang Returns to Nvidia Headquarters to Enthusiastic Employee Cheers
stories.summary: Jensen Huang was welcomed back to Nvidia's Santa Clara headquarters by a massive crowd of cheering employees just days after his abrupt departure. Huang apologized for the turmoil and promised to be a better CEO during his second stint leading the tech giant.

stories.headline: Nvidia Board Unanimously Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
stories.summary: Nvidia's board of directors voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board director effective immediately. The decision follows a review by an independent committee regarding a foreign intelligence investigation, with the board concluding Huang poses no national security risk.

stories.headline: Nato Chief Vows Space Defense Following Reports of Russian Nuclear Satellite
stories.summary: Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte announced that the alliance will protect all allied territory against emerging space threats. The statement follows intelligence reports that Russia is developing a nuclear-armed satellite designed to disrupt or destroy critical orbital infrastructure.

stories.headline: COP31 Climate Summit Collapses Without Reaching Antalya Pacts
stories.summary: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey ended in failure as deep geopolitical divisions prevented nations from agreeing on the central Antalya Pacts. Negotiations broke down over funding disagreements and the omission of explicit fossil fuel phase-out language from the final text. The breakdown has intensified global skepticism regarding whether the UN process can still achieve crucial emissions targets.

stories.headline: ‘Help! My Bible Reading Feels Dead’ – A Call to Revitalize Personal Study
stories.summary: The Gospel Coalition piece addresses the common sense of stagnation in daily Scripture reading and offers practical steps to restore engagement and spiritual vitality.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang’s Nvidia Comeback Serves as a Lesson for Xi on Trump’s Influence
stories.summary: Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia CEO sparked a social‑media frenzy in China, with officials framing it as a vindication of Beijing’s tech stance. The episode underscores how direct U.S.‑China engagement, exemplified by recent Trump‑Xi talks, can shape perceptions of tech policy and espionage narratives.

stories.headline: Nvidia Stock Soars Over 30% as Jensen Huang Returns; Rep. Gomez Resigns Amid Misconduct Claims
stories.summary: Trump touted his role in bringing Huang back, prompting a sharp rally in Nvidia shares. Meanwhile, Democratic Rep. Jimmy Gomez announced his resignation effective Dec. 1 following allegations of sexual misconduct.

stories.headline: Emma Ogier Delivers Compelling Debut Album 'Fly 1111'
stories.summary: Houston singer-songwriter Emma Ogier blends country twang, pop hooks, and indie sensibilities on her debut album, Fly 1111. Released via Lost Highway, the record balances youthful rebellion with sharp, mature storytelling.

stories.headline: Font’s ‘American Bully XL’ Marries Country Heartbreak with Industrial Noise
stories.summary: Texas post‑punk quartet Font’s sophomore album abandons the cryptic swagger of 2024’s Strange Burden for raw, confessional songwriting. The record fuses classic country melancholy with snarling synths, sax and a noise box, pushing Thom Waddill’s ragged vocals through layers of distortion while still delivering moments of tenderness.

stories.headline: Datasette-Charts 0.2a0 Adds Direct Integration with Datasette Agent
stories.summary: The latest update to the datasette-charts plugin introduces integration with Datasette Agent, allowing users to generate charts simply through chat prompts. Users can seamlessly view, build, and interact with data visualizers directly inside their browser windows.

stories.headline: Datasette-Agent 0.7a1 Released With Enhanced Fragment Hash Navigation
stories.summary: The latest pre-release of Datasette Agent improves chat session side panels by supporting navigation via fragment hashes. This update ensures smoother integration with companion plugins like datasette-charts.

stories.headline: Iranian Singer Parastoo Ahmadi and Band Flogged 74 Times for Hijab‑Free Performance
stories.summary: In Qom, authorities administered 74 lashes each to singer Parastoo Ahmadi, three musicians and a producer after a livestreamed concert without a hijab. The court also banned them from audiovisual work and travel for two years, sparking condemnation from artists and human‑rights groups as a violation of basic freedoms.

stories.headline: Polymarket’s California Status Remains Unclear as 2026 Regulations Evolve
stories.summary: CBS Sports reviews the November 2026 landscape, noting that California’s gambling and securities rules still leave the prediction‑market platform in a gray area. The piece outlines pending legislation and recent enforcement actions that could determine whether Polymarket can operate legally in the state.

stories.headline: Finalist Brings Paper‑Style Daily Planner to iPhone Duo
stories.summary: Finalist, a four‑year‑old planning app, launches a dedicated iPhone Duo version that mimics a notebook layout across the dual screens, showing sunrise, moon phase, agenda, timeline and a desk‑clock. Users can drag tasks, customize sections, and rely on on‑device AI to suggest times, delivering a paper‑feel with digital conveniences.

stories.headline: Drone‑Captured Maps Offer New View of Salvage Yards
stories.summary: A project called Salvage Yard Drone uses aerial photography to produce detailed, up‑to‑date maps of metal‑scrap sites, helping operators inventory and plan logistics. The initiative showcases how low‑cost UAVs can automate a traditionally manual, hazardous surveying process.

stories.headline: Gianni Infantino Takes 39 Private‑Jet Trips in 115 Days Amid Re‑Election Scrutiny
stories.summary: Investigations reveal FIFA president Gianni Infantino logged 39 private‑jet flights covering over 102,800 miles and nearly nine days in the air since July, visiting 32 countries. Critics argue the travel, funded by the organization, served his campaign for a second term and raised environmental concerns.

stories.headline: Everton Captain James Tarkowski Receives First Premier League Red, Sparking Debate
stories.summary: In a 4‑0 defeat to Brentford, Tarkowski was shown a second‑yellow turned red after VAR review for a high‑studs challenge, marking his first dismissal after 351 appearances and 74 yellows. The decision cost Everton a key defender for the Merseyside derby and clouded David Moyes’ record‑breaking 593rd match in charge.

stories.headline: UK Nations Confirmed as Joint Hosts of 2035 Women’s World Cup
stories.summary: FIFA has ratified a bid by England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales to stage the 2035 Women’s World Cup across 19 venues, featuring 48 teams and 104 matches over 39 days. The joint bid aligns with a UK government plan to boost female participation in sport and follows recent successful hosting of Euro 2022 and Women’s Euro 2022.

stories.headline: Michigan Drops Trev Alberts, Faces Potential Full Buyout Liability
stories.summary: The university announced it will not appoint former Texas A&M administrator Trev Alberts as athletic director, and legal analysts warn Michigan could be on the hook for the entire buyout stipulated in his contract if the deal is terminated.

stories.headline: Nvidia Shares Slip 8% After Lawmakers Question Trump’s Role in CEO Return
stories.summary: Nvidia’s stock fell nearly 8% on Tuesday amid bipartisan scrutiny of President Trump’s claim that he persuaded the board to reinstate Jensen Huang following his resignation over an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. The dip came despite a prior surge, while rivals AMD, Broadcom and Marvell also slipped amid broader AI‑sector concerns.

stories.headline: Albanian Land for Kushner Resort Mired in Title Fraud Probe
stories.summary: An investigation by Albania’s state prosecutor is examining forged land titles tied to the coastal parcel Jared Kushner intends to develop into a luxury resort, despite Prime Minister Edi Rama’s pledge to push the project forward. Local owners contest the sale, raising doubts about the venture’s legality.

stories.headline: Orioles Trade Trevor Rogers for Freddy Peralta in Fantasy‑Baseball Shake‑up
stories.summary: In a move aimed at bolstering their rotation, the Baltimore Orioles swapped left‑hander Trevor Rogers for right‑hander Freddy Peralta, a change that fantasy owners will need to adjust for as the offseason tracker updates.

stories.headline: CAS Restores Senegal as 2025 AFCON Champions After Legal Battle
stories.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport unanimously ruled that Senegal’s 1‑0 extra‑time victory over Morocco stands, overturning CAF’s earlier decision that stripped the title when Senegal left the field over a disputed penalty. The ruling reaffirms the Teranga Lions as Africa’s 2025 champions.

stories.headline: Trump Calls Nvidia Board Hours Before Huang’s Reinstatement, Sources Say
stories.summary: According to Semafor, President Trump and Vice President JD Vance personally urged Nvidia’s directors to bring back CEO Jensen Huang during a Sunday board meeting, citing his role in open‑source AI. The board voted unanimously, and the stock jumped 30% the next day, despite ongoing regulatory probes.

stories.headline: San Antonio Spurs Coasting on Opponent Injuries
stories.summary: The San Antonio Spurs have rocketed to the top of the NBA's adjusted net ratings with a dominant early-season run. However, analyst Tom Haberstroh notes that their path has frequently benefited from facing shorthanded opponents resting star players.

stories.headline: Restoring a 1982 Japanese ‘Star Wars’ Poster: A Digital Revival
stories.summary: The feature details the meticulous process of rescuing a rare 1982 ‘Star Wars’ movie poster sourced from Japan, using high‑resolution scanning and color correction techniques to bring the vintage artwork back to its original vibrancy for collectors.
